abstract:
Large language models (LLMs) are often considered a ‘tool’ in management research. However, this perspective prevents a deeper
                    systemic
                    understanding of factors leading to their adoption, and how their presence as an epistemic technology transforms the production of management knowledge. We caution against the risk of epistemic substitution through LLMs and adopt a deterministic view of LLMs as an epistemic technology. Developmental System Theory is enlisted to interrogate how LLMs influence (i) the production of management knowledge and (ii) how that influence initiates epistemic feedback loops and practises that reduce the scope of truth and possible knowledge. Doing so advances our understanding of how LLMs keep affecting the research process disadvantageously, with the resultant knowledge concerning
                    social relations in and around work
                    becoming problematic too. Hence, our model constitutes a diagnostic tool to understand how the use of LLMs in research processes endogenously transforms knowledge production in management research –
                    for the worse.
                    In so doing, our model is also a tool of possible remedy, for it highlights that an exclusive focus on LLMs and their effects on the production of management knowledge will be insufficient to undo the negative epistemic feedback loops and practises already set in motion.

title: More than a ‘tool’: A systems-theory perspective on how large language models endogenously transform management knowledge (for the worse)
